sections.title: How does the Aspect ratio calculator work?
sections.html:
The Aspect ratio calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports pixels width (Screen dimensions) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (select aspect ratio); then you type in the pixels height, the AR width, the AR height and the aspect ratio 0.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Aspect ratio calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Pixels width=aspect ratio × pixels height
Pixels width=aspect ratio 0 × pixels height
Pixels width=pixels height × hidden aspect ratio
Custom aspect ratio=AR width ÷ AR height
Custom aspect ratio=pixels width ÷ pixels height
AR width=pixels width ÷ (((pixels width, pixels height)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.html:

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Hidden aspect ratio = 10 and Pixels width = 100 should be roughly the size you expected from I want to calculate set to aspect ratio. and Select aspect ratio set to 16:9 (4K / HD / FHD).

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Aspect ratio calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the pixels height, the AR width and the AR height — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Aspect ratio calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns pixels width (Screen dimensions), derived from the pixels height, the AR width and the AR height. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Aspect ratio calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the pixels height, the AR width and the AR height, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Hidden aspect ratio = 10. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Aspect ratio calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
